{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — APCN 2 Construction & Maintenance Agreement (Teleglobe USA Inc.)

**Prepared by:** In-house counsel (Customer side) 
**Findings reviewed:** 18 rules 
**Status split:** 11 compliant · 4 deviations · 1 missing · 2 needs review

---

## 1. Executive summary

This instrument is a multiparty consortium construction, ownership and maintenance agreement for APCN 2, not a vendor/customer supply or hosting contract. Teleglobe USA Inc. is one of several co-owning Parties with several (not joint) liability, and the equipment Suppliers contract separately with the Procurement Group under the Supply Contract. Several of our standard vendor-facing rules therefore have no counterparty to bind, and we have recorded those as compliant rather than inserting obligations that would bind us symmetrically and work against our interests (notably INSURANCE, WARRANTY, TRANSITION).

The consortium architecture is broadly acceptable to us. Indemnity is mutual and proportionate to each Party's Schedule B Investment Share (Paragraph 21.2, with claim-handling at Paragraphs 32.1–32.4); ownership tracks financial investment with unrestricted circuit assignment and IRU sale rights; assignment is symmetric with consent-free affiliate and successor transfers (Subparagraph 22.3); and there is no exclusivity, non-compete, non-solicit or auto-renewal burden on us. The sole MFN covenant (Subparagraph 15.2) runs in our favour.

Four issues warrant redlines. Two are structural: there is **no aggregate liability cap anywhere in the Agreement**, leaving direct liability unlimited despite the mutual consequential-loss exclusion at Paragraph 21.3; and Paragraph 18 locks us into a **25-year Initial Period with no unilateral exit**, which is the playbook walk-away case for termination for convenience. Two are protective: Paragraph 9.8 confers **uncapped audit rights over our books** with no notice, frequency or auditor-independence limits, and Subparagraph 7.9 imposes a **300% late-payment multiplier** compounded by forfeiture of amounts paid on capacity reclamation under Subparagraph 23.2. Separately, the Agreement contains **no governing law or venue provision at all** — Subparagraph 27.2 deliberately strips connecting factors and Subparagraph 27.1 makes Management Committee referral (with open-ended arbitration discretion) the sole and exclusive remedy.

Two findings could not be completed and require manual review before we rely on this memo as complete (MINCOMMIT, TRANSITION). Three findings (AUDIT, LD, MINCOMMIT) did not pass automated verification and should be confirmed against the source text before the redline goes out.

---

## 2. Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Compliant (at fallback) | KDD T8 | Mutual third-party indemnity at Para 21.2, procedure at Paras 32.1–32.4, capped at each Party's Schedule B Investment Share. IP not expressly enumerated; no procure/modify/replace remedies. |
| Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Compliant | KDD T8 | Ownership tracks investment (§4.3/§12.2, §12.16); unrestricted circuit assignment and IRU sales (§12.4–12.27); no IP or data transfer from us; §31 confidentiality applies. No express IP article (Wet Segment procured under separate Supply Contract, §4.4). |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | KDD T8 | Symmetric; consent-free transfer to successor/Parent/Subsidiary/Affiliate (22.3), reasonableness standard on other consents (22.2), notice only (22.6), successors bound (Para 30). No change-of-control exit right. |
| High | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | KDD T8 | No sourcing or requirements obligation; §§12.20–12.22 confirm freedom to deal with other Carriers. "Sole and exclusive remedy" at §27.1 is a remedies limitation, out of scope. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant (at fallback) | KDD T8 | Terminal Station Right of Use for the term (§11.1), no incremental charges (§11.2), extends to IRU purchasers (§11.5); forfeiture only for uncured non-payment under §23. Contractors not expressly named; not stated as perpetual/irrevocable. |
| High | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete on Customer | Compliant (preferred) | KDD T8 | No restrictive covenant; §11.2 contemplates other cable systems. §§12.1, 12.6–12.15 are asset-use rules applying to all Parties, relaxed by 12.15/12.20/12.22. |
| Medium | MFN — MFN burdening Customer | Compliant (preferred) | KDD T8 | Only MFN is §15.2, binding Terminal Parties; we are an Initial Party and a beneficiary, not an obligor. §17.2 is a non-discrimination duty on Terminal Parties. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Compliant (preferred) | § 21 Relationship of Parties | No solicitation, no-hire or poaching covenant anywhere; § 21 is a bare heading. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and notice window | Compliant | KDD T8 | No auto-renewal or renewal uplift; unilateral exit right at/after the Initial Period (§18.1); ongoing charges are cost-shared O&M (§§6–7). One-year exit notice is longer than preferred but mutual; §18.4 protects a withdrawing Terminal Party. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | KDD T8 | §4.9 disclaimer protects the Procurement Group, which includes us (§3.8). Upstream protection passed through via §§4.6–4.8 and Para 10 maintenance duties with self-help. No inter-Party conformance period or repair/replace remedy. |
| Medium | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Needs review** | — | Automated review did not complete (tool loop exceeded); verification failed. Requires manual analysis. |
| Medium | TRANSITION — Post-termination transition and data return | **Needs review** | KDD T8 | Rule is scoped to services/hosting; no vendor custody of our data (§31.1 mutual; §§9, 10 reciprocal). Consortium exit mechanics exist (§§18.4–18.7, §32.6, §31.4). No data return/certified deletion — deliberately not inserted, as it would bind us and cut against our §9.8/§10 audit and retention rights. |
| Low | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | **Deviation** | KDD T8 | Para 9.8 permits any Party to audit our Segment S/T books with no frequency cap, no notice, no auditor independence or confidentiality, no bar on system access; §9.9 is a procedural gate only. Verification failed — confirm text before sending. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Missing** | KDD T8 | No governing law or venue clause. §27.2 strips connecting factors; §27.1 makes Management Committee referral the sole and exclusive remedy with unspecified arbitration method and seat. Neither preferred nor fallback position met. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | KDD T8 | No vendor relationship; Suppliers sit under the separate Supply Contract. Mutual insurance addressed at §5.3 and §5.1(d); indemnity capped at Schedule B share (§21.2). No coverage limits specified — noted only. |
| Low | LD — Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer | **Deviation** | KDD T8 | §7.9 imposes extended payment charges at 300% of the §7.8 prime-rate reference with no time limit; §23.2 forfeits payment/credit and reimbursement for reclaimed capacity. Both are penalties borne by us. Verification failed — confirm text before sending. |
| Low | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | **Deviation** | KDD T8 | §21.3 mutually excludes indirect/consequential loss (helpful), but no aggregate monetary cap exists anywhere; direct liability is unlimited, failing the fallback. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Deviation** | KDD T8 | §18 imposes a 25-year Initial Period with exit only at/after that period on one year's notice (18.1), or by unanimous agreement (18.2). No Customer convenience right. |

---

## 3. Walk-away items

1. **No Customer termination for convenience in a 25-year term (T4C, §18).** A multi-year lock-in with no unilateral exit is expressly walk-away territory under the playbook. Given the consortium construction-and-maintenance bargain, a 30-day preferred exit would be disproportionate, so we go to the fallback rather than the preferred position.
2. **Unlimited audit rights over our books (AUDIT, Para 9.8).** Audit with no frequency cap, no notice, no auditor independence or confidentiality obligation and no bar on system access is walk-away territory. We address it by insertion rather than by rewriting 9.8, preserving the favourable existing cost allocation and Schedule B proportional recovery.
3. **Unlimited direct liability (LOL-CAP).** The absence of any aggregate cap fails even the fallback (mutual cap with carve-outs) and should be resolved before signature.
4. **No governing law or forum (GOVLAW).** The open-ended arbitration discretion at §27.1, combined with §27.2's removal of connecting factors, leaves both applicable law and seat undetermined and risks a foreign seat.

---

## 4. Next steps

**Redlines to issue (in priority order):**

1. **LOL-CAP —** Insert a new Subparagraph 21.4 imposing a mutual aggregate cap at the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and US$1,000,000, with indemnification, confidentiality, data protection and security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement uncapped, and confirming that amounts due are payment obligations rather than damages. Drafted mutually so we are not disadvantaged relative to the other APCN 2 Parties.
2. **T4C —** Insert a Customer convenience exit on 90 days' notice with any early-termination fee capped at three (3) months' fees, and confine Vendor convenience termination to the end of the then-current term on 90 days' notice (fallback position).
3. **AUDIT —** Insert Paragraph 9.10 applying once-per-12-months, 30 days' prior written notice, business hours, off-site where possible, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, no direct system access, and cost-shifting only on underpayment exceeding 5%. Mutual, so the same limits operate for our benefit.
4. **LD —** Strike the 300% multiplier at §7.9 so late payments accrue at the ordinary §7.8 rate, and convert §23.2's forfeiture on reclamation into a pro-rata credit and reimbursement for capacity not received.
5. **GOVLAW —** Insert a new §27.3 fixing New York governing law and exclusive New York County court jurisdiction, leaving §27.1 and §27.2 otherwise intact.

**Before the redline goes out:**

- Complete the **MINCOMMIT** analysis (minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions) — the automated review did not finish and no conclusion is available.
- Confirm the **AUDIT**, **LD** and **MINCOMMIT** findings against the source text; these did not pass automated verification.
- **TRANSITION —** deal-team input required: if any Party (for example the Network Administrator or Central Billing Party under Annexes 3 and 4) holds Teleglobe operational or billing data in a custodial capacity, we may add a narrow, mutual copy-out right on exit within §18. This should be a deliberate consortium-level amendment, not a unilateral vendor-exit insert.
- Note for the file: the sub-elements recorded in the rationale column above (IP not enumerated in the indemnity, contractors not named in the Right of Use, no inter-Party conformance period, no specified insurance limits, one-year exit notice) are deliberately not redlined and require no negotiation."}
